nodes.label: Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. Before editing docs to correct a status or verification claim, confirm it against ground truth - query the live system with read-only Cypher, run the test, check the artifact - and do not propagate a prose narrative, whether the agent's own, a pasted assessment or a ledger file, as if it were verified. The trigger: in one session the frontend docs were rewritten twice on unverified narratives, first on code-text consistency and then on a pasted assessment that trusted a run.json's stages_done, the exact ledger the status doc had flagged stale with 'trust the graph, not the ledger' - while a direct graph query proved the original working-tree claim exactly right. Confident corrections without verification are the same defect as stale docs. When a doc asserts something verifiable about system state, verify it read-only first; if a source conflicts with the live system, the live system wins and the conflicting source is the thing to flag; and state plainly what was and was not verified. The rule extends to external and changeable facts: training data is NOT current knowledge, so for any fact about software, versions, APIs, library behaviour, pricing or product behaviour, search a current authoritative source and cite it rather than answering from recollection - and when given contradicting evidence, STOP and re-check from a live source rather than doubling down. CANON_AUDIT.md lists this among the grounded, verbatim-quoted and correct desktop entries
